details: Bitcoin (BTC) broke above the significant $80,000 psychological level, reaching its highest point since January 31, 2026. This surge is attributed to a de-escalation of tensions related to Iran, which eased macro headwinds, alongside substantial short liquidations in the crypto market. Institutional conviction and positive ETF flows also contributed to the upward momentum.
title: Bitcoin Surges Past $80,000 Amid Geopolitical De-escalation and Short Squeeze

details: The cryptocurrency market experienced a significant liquidation event, with over $116 million in short positions wiped out in a short period as Bitcoin rapidly ascended to the $80,000 mark.
title: Over $116 Million in Crypto Short Positions Liquidated as Bitcoin Rallies

details: Jerome Powell's anticipated departure as Federal Reserve Chair in May 2026 and Kevin Warsh's nomination have introduced uncertainty into monetary policy, historically linked to Bitcoin price volatility. The Fed's decision to maintain interest rates and declining odds for a June rate cut have already triggered a Bitcoin selloff below $75,000 earlier, though the current rally has overcome this.
title: Federal Reserve Leadership Transition Sparks Bitcoin Volatility Concerns

details: Over $350 million worth of cryptocurrency tokens, including significant amounts of HYPE, ASTER, KITE, and SUI, were scheduled for unlock between late April and May 3, 2026. These token unlock events introduce previously restricted supply into the open market, which can lead to increased market volatility for the affected assets.
title: $350 Million in Crypto Tokens Unlocked, Increasing Market Volatility Potential
